title: 2026 UK grid electricity Scope 2 and T&D QA controls

sources.title: 2026 Government greenhouse gas conversion factors: methodology paper

facts.source_fact: The UK grid factor represents average greenhouse-gas emissions per kWh of electricity generated on the national grid.
Generated electricity emissions are classed as Scope 2 for reporting users.
Transmission and distribution losses are reported separately and classed as Scope 3.
facts.expected_handling: Keep T&D distinct from Scope 2 generation.

facts.source_fact: The calculation incorporates net electricity imports via interconnectors with Ireland, the Netherlands, France, Belgium and Norway.
The direct grid factors include CO2, CH4 and N2O from UK power stations, autogenerators and the imported-electricity proportion.
Fuel-production and fuel-delivery emissions for power stations are not part of the direct grid factor.
facts.expected_handling: Do not mix WTT into direct factor.

facts.source_fact: The grid factor changes year to year as the generation fuel mix and net imports change.
The 2026 methodology uses 2025 electricity data rather than carrying the previous data lag.
Users not revising earlier estimates should recognise that the methodology creates a skip over 2024 electricity-intensity data between the 2025 and 2026 publications.
Generation emissions per unit are obtained by dividing calculated UK electricity-production emissions by electricity generated after the methodology's grid adjustments.
